                        Heavy snowfall causes traffic accidents and chaos across Norway, the Minister of Labour and Inclusion defends her integration remarks by insisting "immigrants are not the problem", and more news on Thursday.

Snow hits Norway, causing road chaos and public transport disruptions

On Tuesday, meteorologists warned that snow was on its way to Norway, with up to 15 centimetres expected in Eastern Norway and up to 30 centimetres in the north.

At first, the snowfall in easter Norway was forecast for Oslo, Akershus, Østfold, Vestfold, and lower Buskerud. However, on Thursday morning, the warning was extended to more areas, and a yellow danger alert now includes Innlandet and Hamar.

A separate snow warning was also issued on Wednesday for parts of Western Norway.

As is often the case, the first heavy snowfall of the season has caused problems across the country. Public transport services have been cancelled, and there have been many road accidents, including several vehicles sliding off slippery roads. For example, a school bus slid off the road in Larvik.

"We are receiving a number of reports of skids, traffic accidents and slippery driving conditions in connection with the recent snowfall," operations manager Per Magne Eftang, from the South-East Police District, wrote in the police log just before 8am, according to daily Aftenposten.

"The snowfall causes changed driving conditions, which in turn change road grip and braking distances. Plan to spend a little longer than usual getting to work and appointments. Drive according to the conditions and keep a good distance from the vehicle in front," he added.

If there was any lingering doubt, you should already have winter tyres fitted if you are driving.

Norwegian vocabulary: trafikkulykker - traffic accidents

READ MORE: How to prepare your car for autumn and winter in Norway

'Immigrants are not the problem', says Norwegian Minister of Labour and Inclusion

Kjersti Stenseng, Minister of Labour and Inclusion, sparked debate in Norway after stating on public broadcaster NRK's programme Debatten that "we have been too naive" regarding integration, pointing out that too many people are out of work, speak too little Norwegian, and live in areas with challenging living conditions.

Her comments triggered pushback from researcher and sociologist Astrid Ouahyb Sundsbø, who questioned in an opinion piece for NRK whether political rhetoric is part of the problem and whether the system built by politicians themselves contributes to exclusion.

"If the government is serious about integration, they must stop with the simple rhetoric that immigrants are the problem, and start doing something about the obstacles inherent in the system they themselves have built," Sundsbø wrote, adding: "Placing the problem with refugees and immigrants not only simplifies politics, it also weakens the basis for solutions."

In response, Stenseng clarified that calling Norway’s past approach "too naive" was aimed at politicians, not at immigrants.

"When I acknowledge that we have been too naive, it is not a criticism of the people who have come here. We have underestimated how difficult it is to succeed with integration. And here, no party is exempt from criticism," she wrote in a follow-up column for NRK.

Stenseng admitted there have been problems in the past, but said that employment and education among people with immigrant backgrounds have improved over the last ten years.

She ended her column by saying the government will present a new national integration strategy in the spring that will focus on workforce participation, living conditions, segregation, and cultural barriers that make integration harder.

Human rights groups criticise Norway over handling of torture survivors in asylum system

A group of human rights organisations has sent a report to the UN Committee against torture, warning that Norway still does not meet its international obligations for asylum seekers and immigration detainees.

The report says that several problems raised in earlier UN reviews still have not been fixed, and that Norway still does not have a required system to identify torture victims among asylum seekers, putting vulnerable people at risk of having their claims wrongly rejected.

The report also criticises the state's five-hour cap on legal aid in standard asylum cases as insufficient when interpreters are needed, alongside concerns over the care of unaccompanied minor asylum seekers, and raises concerns about conditions at the Trandum immigration detention centre.

Jon Ole Martinsen, senior adviser at the Norwegian Organisation for Asylum Seekers (NOAS), told multicultural newspaper Utrop regarding the findings that: "We think it is high time that political decision-makers now initiate the necessary measures to rectify these conditions. It should be absolutely central for Norwegian politicians that we are well within the obligations we have under the Torture Convention."

"We hope that the report will help raise the issues and hopefully eventually lead to changes in practice, and not just political speeches about how important international conventions are and how important it is for Norway to follow them," he added

A cyberattack on software provider Front Systems, which is used by more than 10 percent of clothing stores in Norway, has exposed customer and employee data, according to business daily E24.

The breach happened on November 5th and attackers had access for four hours to the system, giving them time to take about 0.2 percent of the database, including customer names, email addresses and employee login details.

Fortunately, credit card details were not compromised, since payment card data is not stored in the system.

PM Støre falls ill, forced to cancel planned trip to Dublin

At this time of year, many people are getting seasonal illnesses, and Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre is no exception.

On Thursday, Støre was supposed to travel to Dublin to attend the European Political Community (EPC) summit with leaders from about 50 countries, including Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

However, Norwegian newspaper Aftenposten reported that Støre had to cut his plans short and is already flying back home.

                        Snow has arrived across large parts of Norway, bringing a bit of chaos to the cities: from public transport disruptions to damaged cars on the roads and many people unable to reach their destinations.

On Tuesday, meteorologists warned that winter snow was on its way to Norway, with up to 15 centimetres expected in Eastern Norway and up to 30 centimetres in the north.

The snowfall was initially forecast across Oslo, Akershus, Østfold, Vestfold, and lower parts of Buskerud. However, on Thursday morning, the warning was extended to cover several additional areas, with a yellow danger alert now in place for Innlandet and Hamar.

A separate snow warning was also issued on Wednesday for parts of Western Norway.

As is often the case, the first heavy snowfall of the season has caused problems across the country. Public transport services have been cancelled, and there have been many road accidents, including several vehicles sliding off slippery roads.

"It's always surprising how little snow it takes to cause problems. There's always chaos with the first snowfall," said meteorologist Hanne Beate Skattør at the Norwegian Meteorological Institute as reported by newspaper Aftenposten.

"We are receiving a number of reports of skids, traffic accidents and slippery driving conditions in connection with the recent snowfall," operations manager Per Magne Eftang, from the South-East Police District, wrote in the police log just before 8am, according to another article from the daily.

"The snowfall causes changed driving conditions, which in turn change road grip and braking distances. Plan to spend a little longer than usual getting to work and appointments. Drive according to the conditions and keep a good distance from the vehicle in front," he added.

If there was any lingering doubt, you should already have winter tyres fitted if you are driving.

Some of the most notable incidents include dozens of buses cancelled in Vestfold and a school bus sliding off the road in Larvik. "The bus has skidded off the road and into the ditch with all four wheels. There are 24 children on the bus who appear unharmed,"   the police log said, according to public broadcaster NRK.

READ MORE: What you need to know about winter driving in Norway

With the first snowflakes falling in Oslo at 5.30am, public transport delays and traffic disruptions also hit the capital.

According to newspaper VG, over 1,000 bus departures were delayed and 65 percent of bus routes in the area were cancelled.

Oslo police also received several reports of fallen trees damaging parked cars. On the E6 motorway at Skulleruddumpa, two lorries became stuck. "One is facing out of Oslo and the other is facing into Oslo. This is causing some traffic problems at the scene," police reported.

The snowy weather also affected Oslo Airport, causing several delays, although staff from airport operator Avinor said they were working hard to clear the runways.

"There has been a lot of snow at Oslo Airport, so it is in full winter operation. We are ploughing continuously. It is quite normal under such conditions that there will also be some delays in air traffic. All the planes also have to go through de-icing before they can take off," communications adviser Helena W. Jensen at Avinor told NRK.

Brannstedet er så nær jernbanelinjen at strømmen til jernbanelinjen måtte tas, opplyser politiet. Jernbanen er stengt i påvente av at brannvesenet får slukket brannen helt.

articles.title: CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi
articles.content:
Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.

Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.

Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.

Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.

Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.

Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.

Fra 20. januar 2025 er Donald Trump igjen president i USA, hvor det bor mer enn 330 millioner mennesker fordelt på 50 stater.

articles.content:
Minst seks personer skal være drept og flere såret i et israelsk luftangrep mot Nasser-sykehuset i Khan Younis sør på Gazastripen natt til torsdag.

Det opplyser en talsperson for det Hamas-kontrollerte sivilforsvaret i Gaza til Reuters.

Angrepet rammet en bygning som huser kirurgisk avdeling ved sykehuset i Khan Younis, og forårsaket omfattende ødeleggelser, ifølge talsperson Mahmoud Basal.

Det israelske militæret har foreløpig ikke kommentert hendelsen.

Israel har den siste tiden trappet opp angrepene mot Gazastripen og hevder at Hamas forsøker å omgruppere styrkene og fylle opp våpenlagrene.

Krigen i Gaza

Konflikten mellom Israel og Hamas eskalerte etter angrepet fra Hamas 7. oktober 2023. Siden har Israel ført krig mot Gaza, hvor Hamas regjerer. Over 65.000 palestinere er drept, og FN har slått alarm om katastrofal sult i Gaza.

Det er ikke meldt om savnede personer og alle som skal bo på stedet er evakuert.

Fuglaas ber publikum om å holde avstand slik at nødetatene kommer frem til brannen.

Brannen kan sees på lang avstand, skriver operasjonslederen.

                        Welfare agency Nav under fire over sickness and disability benefits, the Storting rejects proposal for mandatory "integration contracts", and more news from Norway on Wednesday.

Newspaper VG reported on Tuesday that the EFTA Court has concluded that Norwegian disability rules break EEA free-movement law.

Under the National Insurance Act and welfare agency Nav's regulations, EEA citizens need five years of continuous social security coverage to qualify for disability benefits in Norway.

The court pointed out that in many European countries, social security rights come from employment, but in Norway, just living legally is enough. So, demanding uninterrupted coverage creates an unfair barrier for people who move between countries for work.

The case was referred to the EFTA Court after a Spanish and a German citizen were denied disability benefits from Nav despite living in Norway for several years. The two men, originally from Pakistan and Morocco, arrived in Norway in 2013 and 2005,  and both became disabled three years after their arrival.

The attorney representing the Spanish citizen told news agency NTB: "It is not just Nav that has been wrong. It is the law itself that is in conflict with EEA law. It is worrying that Norway still has not cleaned up how EEA rules are followed in the area of social security"

State Secretary Line Eldring from the Ministry of Labour and Social Inclusion disagreed and maintained that the current rules comply with the EEA Agreement.

Norwegian vocabulary: å bli ufør - to become disabled

Nav faces further scrutiny over sickness benefit errors

Criticism of welfare agency Nav continued after the Office of the Auditor General released a report exposing that Norway's automated welfare system used the wrong salary baseline to calculate sickness benefits in more than half of first-time cases.

According to newspaper Aftenposten, the audit found that until June this year, automated errors affected the income baseline in 57 percent of first-time sickness benefit decisions.

It also showed that in 73 percent of cases where the system flagged possible payment errors, caseworkers did not provide written explanations, and the decisions were not changed or checked by a person.

"The fact that Nav's case processing systems do not ensure that sickness benefit payments follow the laws and regulations is a serious weakness in a system that processes large sums. It is worthy of criticism," said Auditor General Karl Eirik Schjøtt-Pedersen.

Norwegian vocabulary: sykepenger - sickness benefit

Storting rejects FrP proposal for mandatory integration contracts

Norway's parliament has turned down a proposal from the right-wing Progress Party (FrP) to introduce mandatory integration contracts for "non-Western" refugees, asylum seekers, and family reunification applicants.

During the vote, other parties questioned whether the proposal was legal, whether it might go against anti-discrimination laws, and pointed out that "non-Western" countries were not clearly defined without a straight answer from the Progress Party, as reported by multicultural newspaper Utrop.

They also explained that an official integration declaration will already take effect on January 1st, 2027.

If the proposal had passed, people in these groups could have faced penalties such as losing their residence permits, financial support or being denied citizenship if they did not follow the contract, Norwegian laws and secular values, such as gender equality and freedom of expression.

Read more about the proposal: Norwegian parliament set to consider two key immigration proposals

That same day, the Storting also rejected another proposal from the opposition party. This one would have made immigrants and refugees pay for public interpretation services themselves after living in Norway for three years.

READ MORE: Norway sets tougher new integration requirements for refugees

Royal Palace announces consecration date for Norway's new King and Queen

According to a press release from the royal house, King Haakon and Queen Mette-Marit will be consecrated at Nidaros Cathedral in Trondheim on Sunday, August 22nd, 2027.

The ceremony (called kongesigning in Norwegian) is a traditional religious service where the monarchs receive the Church of Norway's blessing to mark their reign.

As Norway ended formal coronations in 1908, King Olav V started the consecration tradition in 1958, and King Harald V and Queen Sonja continued it in 1991.

The ceremony in Trondheim will also kick off a two-year tour aboard the Royal Yacht Norge, with the royal couple visiting communities across the country until 2028.

Norwegian vocabulary: å signe - to bless or consecrate

​Ukrainian President may open office for air defence project in Oslo

Ukrainian President Zelensky is in Denmark meeting with Nordic leaders, where he stated that Ukraine is exploring the possibility of opening defence offices in both Denmark and Norway.

"We are going to talk about opening an office in Denmark and also in Oslo. I think it could happen within a month," the president told Danish broadcasters.

The offices would coordinate work on Freyja, a European anti-missile system currently under development as an alternative to the American Patriot air defence system, as reported by Norwegian public broadcaster NRK.

Norwegian vocabulary: luftforsvarssystem - air defence system

                        As of November 10th, passengers flying with Europe's biggest budget airline must check their luggage at least an hour before departure.

If you've got a Ryanair flight on the calendar take note: As of November 10th, Europe's biggest budget airline will be closing airport bag drop services 60 minutes before all scheduled flights.

This means that passengers are required to hand over any checked luggage at the Ryanair service desks at the airport at least an hour before their flight. Previously these services remained open until at least 40 minutes before flights' scheduled departure.

According to a statement shared by the airline, the move is intended to ensure that passengers who do check in luggage have more time to clear airport security and passport control, and reach their departure gate before boarding begins.

Ryanair suggests the new policy will help reduce the number of passengers who miss their flights due to delays at airport security or passport control.

Many European airports have seen longer-than-usual queues following the roll-out of EES checks. Media reports have highlighted cases where passengers were left behind due to such delays, even after their luggage was checked-in.

About 20 percent of Ryanair passengers check in baggage. The remaining 80 percent of passengers who don’t check in bags will be unaffected by the change.

For passengers travelling with Ryanair, it's important to understand the airline's latest policies to avoid being charged additional fees.

Last year the airline stopped issuing printed boarding passes for free, requiring passengers to check-in in advance online or with the airline's app, or else be hit with a check-in fee to have the ticket printed at the counter.

Recently, Ryanair CEO Michael O'Leary told investors that the airline would likely bring "double-digit" price increases on airfares across Europe in 2027 due primarily to high fuel prices.

articles.title: FNs generalsekretær: - Det viktigste er å fortelle sannheten om klimaet
articles.content:
FNs generalsekretær António Guterres åpnet onsdag høynivåmøtet på klimatoppmøtet i Antalya.

– Det viktigste vi gjør er å fortelle sannheten om klimautviklingen. De siste fire årene har vært de varmeste på kloden noensinne.

Guterres sa at for å redde planeten må vi øke tempoet i utfasingen av fossil energi.

– Kull må være borte om 15 år, og bruken av olje og gass må kuttes med en tredjedel, sa FN-sjefen.

– Vi må bidra slik at de fattige landene også kan nå målet med å erstatte fossil energi med fornybar, før det er for sent.

Guterres sa at de som profitterer mest på fossil energi må bidra mest.

Han pekte på de enorme overskuddene til oljeselskapene, og sammenlignet dem med «den relativt beskjedne summen» som er gitt til fondet for tap og skade for sårbare land.

– Det er på tide at regjeringer skattlegger disse selskapene og bruker pengene til å hjelpe sårbare land med å komme seg på beina igjen.

Klima og miljø

Verden opplever allerede klimaendringene, slår FNs klimapanel fast. Mer ekstremvær, høyere havnivå og økte helseproblemer er noen av konsekvensene, ifølge deres siste hovedrapport.

De forente nasjoner (FN)

FN ble opprettet like etter andre verdenskrig, i hovedsak for å unngå lignende krigssituasjoner i framtiden. Hovedkontoret ligger i New York i USA, og organisasjonen har 193 medlemsland.

FNs klimapanel

I september 2013 la FNs klimapanel fram sin mest omfattende klimarapport noen sinne. Den viste at forskerne er hele 95 prosent sikre på at global oppvarming skyldes oss. Natt til 31. mars 2014 legges andre delrapport fram.

                        If you want to complete your Norwegian social studies or citizenship test before the end of 2026 and keep your immigration or residency process moving, you are still in time to secure a place.

Whether you are preparing to apply for Norwegian citizenship or need the social studies test for your permanent residency, test centres across Norway still have dates open in November and early December. This represents the final opportunity before the designated sites close for the Christmas holidays.

If you need your test results ready to submit your paperwork in early 2027, you should book immediately, as next year's dates have not been published yet.

On the other hand, if you are not in a rush, the Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) accepts registrations year-round, so it may be better to wait for the next round.

READ MORE: How hard is it to pass Norway’s citizenship and social studies tests?

Dates and availability vary across the country. In Oslo, for example, slots are still open on November 13th and December 4th for both tests, while in Bergen, only December 1st is available for the moment.

However, unless you are legally entitled to take the test for free (for example, if you have protection under the Introduction Act), you will need to pay an exam fee. Because of this, it may be better to take the test only if you feel fully prepared.

The fee varies by municipality and county, usually between 900 and 1,300 kroner per exam.

If you feel confident and wish to sit the test, you can book your place here.

articles.title: Bussjåfør dømt til fem års fengsel for overgrep mot sårbare barn på skolerute i Vestfold
articles.content:
En mann i 60-årene fra Vestfold er i Vestfold tingrett dømt til fem års ubetinget fengsel for grov voldtekt av to jenter under 14 år, skriver Østlands-Posten.

Overgrepene skjedde inne i en skolebuss på en rute for elever med spesielle behov i Vestfold, høsten 2024. Ifølge dommen utnyttet sjåføren jentenes sårbarhet ved å gjøre ureglementerte stopp på rasteplasser langs ruten for å forgripe seg på dem, til tross for at jentene forsøkte å be ham om å slutte.

Politiet ble varslet i fjor vinter etter at jentene fortalte foreldrene sine om hendelsene.

Mannen erkjente straffskyld da saken var oppe i retten. Retten la i skjerpende retning vekt på at overgrepene var planlagte og at han grovt misbrukte sin tillitsrolle som yrkessjåfør med ansvar for barnas trygghet.

I tillegg til fengselsstraffen er mannen dømt til å betale 300.000 kroner i oppreisning til hver av jentene. Han ilegges også et femårig kontaktforbud, og fradømmes retten til å kjøre persontransport for alltid. Forsvareren opplyser at dommen ikke vil bli anket.

                            The Progress Party (Frp), Norway’s most right-wing parliamentary party, is pushing two separate measures in the Storting to impose tighter conditions on foreign arrivals. Photo by Sincerely Media on Unsplash

                        Norway’s parliament, the Storting, will debate and vote on two different immigration and integration proposals this week.

Both proposals were put forward by the right-wing opposition Progress Party (Frp); however, a majority in parliament is needed for either proposal to move to the next step and become law.

The first proposal would introduce a required and binding “integration contract” for non-Western refugees, asylum seekers, and people arriving for family reunification.

Under the plan, newcomers would have to formally agree to follow Norwegian laws and secular values, such as gender equality and freedom of expression, alongside strict rules regarding child-rearing and employment. Refusing to sign the integration contract would result in immediate deportation, while breaching its terms could lead to cuts in welfare benefits.

The Progress Party defended the proposal by pointing out that Denmark introduced similar contractual integration measures in 2019, while warning against Sweden’s struggles with integration as an example of what Norway must avoid.

The second measure seeks to introduce mandatory user fees for public interpretation services.

According to the Progress Party’s plan, foreign residents would have to pay out of pocket for interpreters when dealing with public services after living in Norway for three years. The party says that using state-funded interpreters for too long makes people less likely to learn Norwegian.

articles.title: How will a breakup affect your Norwegian family immigration residence rights?
articles.content:
Add a comment
                                                                                            
                                        
                                                                        
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                    
                                        
                                            
                                        
                                    
                                
                            
                        
                    
                    
                    
                            
                            Here's what happens to your residence rights if you and your partner separate. Pictured is a Norwegian flag. Photo by Herbert Grambihler on Unsplash
                    
                                            
                            
        
            
            
            
            
        
        Add The Local as a preferred source
    
                        
                                        
                        One of the most common residence permit types is the Norwegian family immigration permit, which allows non-EEA nationals the right to move to Norway to be with a spouse or partner. But what happens to your residence rights if you separate?

To legally live and work in Norway, those from outside the EEA will typically need a Norwegian residence permit. These are granted by Norway’s immigration authority, the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI), for several reasons.

These range from working in Norway to studying or moving to the country to be with a family member or a partner.

To be granted a family immigration permit to move to the country to be with a partner, several conditions will need to be met, such as the age requirements, needing to have been in a relationship for a set amount of time and payment of an application fee.

However, as the permit is granted on the condition that you are moving to Norway to be with the person you are in a relationship with, what happens if your marriage breaks down or you and your partner separate?

Will you lose your residence rights and have to leave Norway? The answer, according to the UDI, will depend on your situation.

“When a person with a family immigration permit with a spouse/cohabitant/registered partner separates, they do not lose the right to stay in Norway immediately but must inform the UDI about the change in status as soon as possible. They will have the right to stay in Norway until UDI has made a decision of revocation,” a spokesperson for the UDI informed The Local.

This means that when you report the separation to immigration services, the UDI will look into your case on an individual basis and decide whether you will be able to stay in Norway.

The person in question will also be able to stay in the country provided they meet the conditions for a different type of permit. This can be for, say, work or education. Sometimes, this may be easier said than done, as work permits are not granted for any job.

Typically, they are granted to skilled workers for a role that requires education or training that makes them qualified for that specific role. You can read more about the specifics of a work permit here.

If you choose the study permit route, you must demonstrate that you have been admitted to an approved educational institution and have sufficient funds to cover your living costs. However, keep in mind that this route also brings other types of limitations, as a study permit only grants part-time work rights (typically up to 20 hours per week).

Another family immigration permit is another option for those with a child in Norway. Then they will need to exchange their family immigration permit for one that sees the applicant live in Norway to be with a child.

This applies to those with a child in Norway who either have custody for or partial custody with visitation rights. You can read more about applying to be with a child in Norway here.

If you do not meet the requirements for other permits, then the UDI will assess whether you are eligible for a work permit on other grounds, such as having a solid connection to Norway, or if there are humanitarian considerations in your case or you are a national protected against deportation to your home country.

Additionally, if you or your child have been abused by your spouse or cohabitant, you can instead apply for another type of residence permit.

Typically, the UDI does not renew the permits of those who have divorced or separated from their partners, so this route only seems possible in exceptional circumstances.

Those at risk of losing their permit are notified about the review and if their residence rights are being revoked. Should the UDI decide that your residence rights are being withdrawn, the UDI will invite the person in question to write a reply and explain their view of the case, and whether there is anything the UDI hasn’t considered.

Legal assistance is provided to write the reply, and fees are covered by the state, regardless of whether the decision is overturned or not.

If a permit is revoked, the decision can also be appealed, and the person in question will have access to legal assistance. Should the appeal fail, then you may be issued a deadline to leave Norway. You can read more about the revocation of a residence permit here.

If you have already lived in Norway for three years, you might think you can apply for permanent residence after separating. However, this may not work because your current permit must still be valid and you must still meet its main conditions when the decision is made.

If you are no longer living together with your partner, you do not meet the requirements of your family permit, and your application will be rejected.

Many foreigners also mistakenly believe that the one-year separation period, which usually applies in Norway, especially when children are involved, counts toward the  time requirement for permanent residence. However, in short, it does not.

According to Norwegian immigration rules, your family permit is no longer valid as soon as the relationship ends and you stop living together. You can stay in Norway legally while UDI reviews your case, but any time spent living apart from your partner does not count toward permanent residence.

In any case, it is always a good idea to consult an immigration lawyer if you find yourself in this situation so they can guide you on your best options.

En mann i 20-årene er dømt til 11 måneders fengsel etter å ha hatt samleie med en jente som var plassert på en barnevernsinstitusjon.

Mannen var innleid som nattevakt på institusjonen da han i løpet av to netter sommeren 2024 hadde samleie med den mindreårige jenta, skriver Romerikes Blad.

Mannen har erkjent samleiene, men nekter straffskyld. Han hevdet at jenta hadde tatt initiativet. Romerike og Glåmdal tingrett dømte mannen til 11 måneders fengsel.

Han må også betale 120.000 kroner i oppreisning og forbys å arbeide ved barnevernsinstitusjoner i tre år fra rettskraftig dom.

Mannens forsvarer, advokat Anne Merete Evenrud, opplyser at det foreløpig ikke er tatt stilling til om dommen skal ankes.

articles.title: Norge gir 600 regnskogmillioner til Brasil
articles.content:
Klimaminister Sigrun Aasland (Ap) har med en stor sjekk når hun mandag reiser til åpningen av klimatoppmøtet i Tyrkia.

– Vi har med 600 millioner kroner til Brasil, for de har levert veldig gode resultater på å hindre avskoging i 2025, sier Aasland.

Brasil har det siste året redusert avskogningen til det laveste nivået siden målingene staret for over 40 år siden.

Gjennom den norske regnskogsatsingen gir Norge økonomisk støtte til Brasil når de klarer å redusere avskogingen.

– Norge finansierer resultater, og nå har vi med oss finansiering av de gode resultatene i Brasil, sier Aasland.

Klima og miljø

Verden opplever allerede klimaendringene, slår FNs klimapanel fast. Mer ekstremvær, høyere havnivå og økte helseproblemer er noen av konsekvensene, ifølge deres siste hovedrapport.

Brasil

President Lula da Silva vant presidentvalget i Brasil i oktober og ble innsatt 1. januar 2023. 8. januar gikk støttespillere av tidligere president Jair Bolsonaro til angrep på Kongressen, presidentpalasset og høyesterett i hoevdstaden Brasília.

Amazonas

Regnskogen i Amazonas er truet av avskoging og branner. Regnskogen inneholder svært mange arter, og den binder også store mengder CO2, som frigjøres når skogen brenner.

articles.content:

Lørdag formiddag opplyste Slottet på nettsidene sine at «statsrådet forestår bestyrelsen av riket».

Ifølge nettsidene var kongen og kronprinsessen på privat opphold i utlandet. Det betyr at regjeringen har ansvaret for å styre og forvalte landet.

articles.title: Rødt vil halvere pengestøtten til ungdomspartiet
articles.content:
De siste årene har Rød Ungdom mottatt 2 millioner kroner fra moderpartiet, men nå har landsstyret bestemt seg for å redusere pengestøtten.

Landsstyret i Rødt falt søndag ned på å kutte støtten til ungdomspartiet, ifølge Vårt Land. Partileder Marie Sneve Martinussen forklarer at Rødt er et parti i vekst, og at det stiller kandidater til valg i flere kommuner enn før neste år.

– Det er først og fremst veldig gledelig, men gir også økte utgifter. Derfor har Landsstyret i Rødt vedtatt et budsjett som prioriterer lokalvalgkamp og skolering for å gjøre Rødt så store og sterke at vi ikke er til å komme utenom over hele landet, sier Martinussen til avisen.

Partiet Rødt

Partiet Rødt ble stiftet i mars 2007 på grunnlag av Rød Valgallianse og AKP, med Rød ungdom som ungdomsorganisasjon. I 2025 gjorde partiet sitt beste valg noensinne, med 5,3 prosent oppslutning.

Rød Ungdom

Rød Ungdom (RU) er ungdomsorganisasjonen til partiet Rødt. Organisasjonen ble grunnlagt i 1963, og hadde tidligere navnet Sosialistisk Ungdomsforbund. I 2024 ble Amrit Kaur valgt til leder i RU.
